sections.title_ar: قيد الوحدات البحرية المعفاة من التسجيل

verification_methodology_note: PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS: laws.boe.gov.sa's LIVE portal was unreachable this pass (direct HTTPS curl to the exact law-detail URL [https://laws.boe.gov.sa/BoeLaws/Laws/LawDetails/43344715-1e0d-4e7f-9895-aa3d00f670e6/1] returned 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' / curl exit code 35, on both the HTML law page and the BOE-hosted official English-translation PDF download link, repeated). HOWEVER, Wayback Machine snapshots of BOTH the exact BOE law-detail page (timestamped 20251212225734) AND the BOE-hosted official English-translation PDF download link (timestamped 20250403045231) WERE reachable this pass -- for BOTH resources the https:// scheme succeeded (HTTP 200) while the plain http:// scheme returned HTTP 403 for the same snapshots; both schemes were tried per this corpus's established practice and whichever worked was used, with no hostname tricks or bypass beyond the two established proxies (Wayback Machine / r.jina.ai -- r.jina.ai was not needed this pass since direct Wayback fetches succeeded). The archived BOE Arabic law page was parsed with BeautifulSoup (not naive regex/tag-stripping), locating each of 391 'article_item' divs and its 'HTMLContainer' child, recovering the complete text of all 391 articles, the decree number/date (مرسوم ملكي رقم (م/33) وتاريخ 1440/04/05هـ, corresponding to 12 December 2018G; Council of Ministers Resolution No. 197 dated 4/4/1440H; published in the Official Gazette 28/4/1440H corresponding to 4 January 2019G), and BOE's own per-article HTML class attributes -- all 391 'article_item' divs carry ONLY the class 'no_alternate' (BOE's no-op/default marker), with zero occurrences of any amended ('مادة معدلة') or repealed ('مادة ملغية') marker class anywhere on the page, even though the page's legend explicitly defines both marker classes (confirming BOE's template supports flagging amendments/repeals but none are applied to this law). This is corroborated by BOE's own page-level 'الحالة' (status) field reading 'ساري' (in force). BOE's heading structure was also parsed in full document order (h3.center headings interleaved with article_item divs) to reconstruct the law's باب/فصل/subsection hierarchy -- see the chapter_structure field and the notes on its reconstruction below. SECONDARY CROSS-VERIFICATION: nezams.com (fetched live, directly, with a standard browser User-Agent header, ~3.9MB page containing all 391 'li.subject' article items) provided an independent HTML transcription of all 391 articles under identical Arabic ordinal article headers. A full programmatic text comparison of all 391 articles between the BOE-via-Wayback text and the nezams.com text (after Unicode NFC normalization and normalizing a small number of purely-cosmetic whitespace/punctuation variants -- non-breaking space U+00A0 vs regular space in 27 articles, and a curly-quote vs straight-quote rendering of the classification-society name 'أياكس' in Article 30) found EXACT agreement on 381 of 391 articles, with the remaining 10 articles (Articles 316-325, within الباب السابع / الفصل الأول: التأمين البحري -- الأحكام العامة) showing that nezams.com's page repeats -- verbatim -- the content of Articles 306-315 in place of the genuinely distinct provisions that belong at Articles 316-325 (a nezams.com site-side content-duplication bug, not a BOE or extraction artifact; see known_unresolved_discrepancies for the full analysis and the independent third-source resolution). nezams.com's own dedicated 'التعديلات' (amendments) metadata field independently states 'لم يجرى عليه تعديل' (no amendment has been made to it), matching BOE's lack of any per-article amendment marker; its 'الملحقات' (attachments) field is empty, consistent with this Law spawning multiple separate implementing regulations rather than one single referenced Implementing Regulation (see known_unresolved_discrepancies). THIRD INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION: BOE's own official English-translation PDF of this Law (98 pages, fetched via the same Wayback Machine snapshot mechanism from BOE's own 'Files/Download' endpoint, i.e. an entirely separate BOE-hosted document from the Arabic HTML law page) was downloaded and read in full via pdftotext. Its 391 sequentially-numbered 'Article N' sections independently confirm the same article count, the same باب/chapter divisions and titles (rendered in English), and -- critically -- independently confirm the content and sequential distinctness of Articles 316-325 (i.e., that BOE's Arabic is correct and nezams.com's duplicate rendering for that range is the erroneous one). This English translation was used ONLY for structural/content cross-checking, NEVER as a source of Arabic wording; no translation, paraphrase, or back-translation into Arabic was performed anywhere in this track. TWO FURTHER SOURCES ATTEMPTED, INCONCLUSIVE: qistas.com's legislation viewer page for this Law returned only a short, apparently access-gated preview (~2.6KB of text, covering only Article 1) insufficient for any further cross-check; qanoniah.com's page is a JavaScript-rendered single-page application that returned no usable static text via a direct fetch. Neither contradicted anything found; neither contributed additional verification. AMENDMENT STATUS: this Royal Decree (M/33, 5/4/1440H) has NEVER been amended since enactment, per BOE (zero per-article amendment markers across all 391 articles), nezams.com (explicit 'لم يجرى عليه تعديل' statement), and a targeted web search for any amending Royal Decree (none found) alike -- all 391 articles are recorded as اصلية (original), with no مكرر (bis) articles anywhere (confirmed by the total absence of 'مكرر' in any of BOE's 391 article headers). SUPERSESSION: Article 391 (the Law's final closing article) expressly repeals 'الباب الثاني من نظام المحكمة التجارية' (Book Two of the Commercial Court Regulation, issued by Royal Decree No. 32 dated 15/1/1350H) and 'نظام الموانئ والمرافئ والمنائر البحرية' (the Ports, Harbours and Lighthouses Law, issued by Royal Decree M/27 dated 24/6/1394H), plus 'كل ما يتعارض معه من أحكام' (any other conflicting provisions) -- this repeal clause is preserved verbatim in Article 391's text and is corroborated by multiple secondary English-language legal-update sources (Al Tamimi & Co., Lexology, Mondaq) independently describing the same predecessor-repeal scope. No exhaustive article-by-article diff against the repealed predecessor instruments' own text was performed this pass (see known_unresolved_discrepancies). COMPANION IMPLEMENTING REGULATIONS: Article 390 requires the Chairman (see the terminology note in known_unresolved_discrepancies regarding 'الرئيس' vs the Article-1-defined term 'الوزير') to issue 'اللوائح اللازمة للنظام' (the regulations necessary for the Law) within 180 days of publication -- note the PLURAL 'اللوائح', consistent with this Law having spawned MULTIPLE separate implementing regulations issued by the General Authority for Transport (الهيئة العامة للنقل, GAT/TGA) rather than one single consolidated Implementing Regulation, including (per this pass's web search, not independently fetched/ingested) a vessel-registration regulation, a regulation governing the practice of maritime transport business, and a maritime-ticket-sales regulation, among others. Consistent with this corpus's established precedent for prior tracks (finance_lease_law, healthcare_professions_law, etc.), this track ingests ONLY the primary 391-article Law; the companion regulations are flagged as follow-up candidates, not fabricated or partially guessed at. No legal text is altered by choice; a small number of purely-cosmetic whitespace/punctuation normalizations (non-breaking-space-to-space; curly-to-straight quotation marks; Unicode NFC normalization of combining-diacritic order) were applied uniformly and are documented in known_unresolved_discrepancies -- none change any word, character sequence (beyond the whitespace/quote-glyph/diacritic-order changes described), or legal meaning. Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation was performed on the Arabic text (the BOE English PDF was used only for structural/content cross-checking, never as a source of Arabic wording). Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: nezams.com's independently-fetched live HTML transcription of this Law repeats -- verbatim, byte-for-byte -- the content it renders for Articles 306-315 in place of the content it renders under the labels 'المادة السادسة عشرة بعد الثلاثمائة' through 'المادة الخامسة والعشرون بعد الثلاثمائة' (Articles 316-325). This was identified by a full programmatic diff of all 391 articles between BOE-via-Wayback and nezams.com: nezams.com's rendering for label '316' is textually identical to its own rendering for label '306', its rendering for label '317' identical to its own '307', and so on through '325'/'315' -- a clean +10 duplication offset, consistent with a nezams.com template/CMS bug that repeated one HTML block rather than rendering the genuinely distinct next ten articles. This is NOT treated as a discrepancy in the primary legal text: BOE-via-Wayback-Machine's Arabic HTML (the primary source for this track) renders Articles 316-325 as ten internally coherent, topically sequential, and mutually distinct marine-insurance provisions (duty to safeguard insured items upon peril; settlement of damage by indemnity; insurer not obliged to repair/replace; insurer's share of general average; rules on partial/conditional abandonment; notice of abandonment; disclosure of other policies; forfeiture for bad-faith false claims; subrogation; and the two-year limitation period) -- and this exact sequence and content is INDEPENDENTLY confirmed, article-by-article, by BOE's own official English-translation PDF (Articles 316 through 325, read in full via pdftotext this pass), which is a wholly separate BOE-hosted document from the Arabic HTML page and could not have inherited nezams.com's duplication bug. This track therefore adopts BOE's Arabic text for Articles 316-325 with high confidence (2-source agreement: BOE Arabic + BOE's own official English translation) and flags nezams.com as unreliable for this specific 10-article range only -- consistent with this corpus's established precedent of flagging nezams.com as unreliable for isolated ranges in other tracks (e.g. customs_law_nezams_unreliable) rather than discarding it wholesale, since it agreed exactly with BOE on the other 381 of 391 articles.

Article 390 requires 'الرئيس' to issue 'اللوائح اللازمة للنظام' (the regulations -- plural -- necessary for the Law) within 180 days of publication. Consistent with the plural wording, a web search this pass found this Law has spawned MULTIPLE separate implementing regulations issued by the General Authority for Transport (الهيئة العامة للنقل), including (non-exhaustively, per secondary-source mentions only, none independently fetched or ingested this pass): a vessel-registration and floating-unit-recording regulation (لائحة تسجيل السفن وقيد الوحدات البحرية, seen hosted at old.tga.gov.sa/Regulations/Read/2186), a regulation governing the licensed practice of maritime transport business (لائحة مزاولة أعمال النقل البحري, old.tga.gov.sa/Regulations/Read/2187), a maritime-travel-ticket-sales regulation, and small-vessel-inspection / portable-rescue-equipment-maintenance regulations mentioned by secondary sources. nezams.com's own 'الملحقات' (attachments) metadata field for this Law is empty (no single regulation is cross-referenced there), consistent with there being no ONE consolidated Implementing Regulation to point to. Consistent with this corpus's established precedent (finance_lease_law, healthcare_professions_law, cooperative_health_insurance_law, and others), this track ingests ONLY the primary 391-article Law; the companion regulation(s) are flagged as a follow-up candidate, not fabricated or partially guessed at.

Article 1's definitions list (item 2) defines the term 'الوزير' (literally 'the Minister') as 'وزير النقل، رئيس مجلس إدارة هيئة النقل العام' (the Minister of Transport, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Public Transport Authority) -- 'الوزير' is the ONLY term matching this office defined in Article 1, and the word 'الوزير' itself appears exactly once in the entire 391-article text (within this very definition). Five operative articles (8, 30, 222, 257, and 390) instead use the word 'الرئيس' ('the Chairman' / 'the President') -- a word never separately defined in Article 1 -- to refer to what is, from context and from BOE's own official English translation (which renders Article 1 item 2 simply as 'Chairman: Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Public Transport Authority', dropping the 'Minister of Transport' portion of the Arabic definition entirely in its own English short-form label), evidently the same office. This word choice ('الرئيس' in five operative articles vs. 'الوزير' in the Article-1 definition) was verified to be the law's genuine primary-source text, NOT an extraction artifact of this pass's own tooling: the identical word 'الرئيس' in the identical five articles is present in BOTH BOE-via-Wayback-Machine's HTML (parsed with BeautifulSoup this pass) AND in nezams.com's independently live-fetched HTML transcription of the same five articles (also fetched this pass, from an entirely separate site with its own separate scraping pipeline). This track preserves both words exactly as they appear in the primary source, in their respective articles, without altering, harmonizing, or annotating the text itself; this entry documents the terminological looseness transparently rather than silently normalizing it or guessing at legislative intent.

BOE's archived HTML rendered a small number of inter-word spaces as non-breaking-space characters (U+00A0) rather than regular spaces (found in 27 of 391 articles after cross-diffing against nezams.com's independent transcription, which used regular spaces at the same positions), and rendered the classification-society name 'أياكس' in Article 30 with curly/typographic quotation marks (\u201c \u201d) where nezams.com used straight ASCII quotation marks. Both are purely presentational/whitespace-glyph differences with zero effect on wording or legal meaning; this track normalizes non-breaking spaces to regular spaces and curly quotes to straight quotes uniformly across all 391 articles (and applies Unicode NFC normalization to resolve a combining-diacritic-order difference observed between the two sources' rendering of shadda+fatha sequences, e.g. in 'إلاَّ'), consistent with this corpus's established practice of documenting -- rather than silently performing -- such text-hygiene normalizations (see e.g. finance_lease_law's and customs_law's own documented encoding-artifact fixes). No word, digit, or substantive character sequence was added, removed, or reordered by this normalization.

Article 391 (this Law's final article) expressly repeals 'الباب الثاني من نظام المحكمة التجارية' (Book Two of the Commercial Court Regulation, Royal Decree No. 32 dated 15/1/1350H) and 'نظام الموانئ والمرافئ والمنائر البحرية' (the Ports, Harbours and Lighthouses Law, Royal Decree M/27 dated 24/6/1394H), plus any other conflicting provisions -- this repeal clause text is preserved verbatim from BOE/nezams and is corroborated by multiple secondary English-language legal-update sources (e.g. Al Tamimi & Co., Lexology, Mondaq), which independently describe this Law as replacing 'Articles 150 to 431' of the Commercial Court Regulation alongside the Ports, Harbours and Lighthouses Regulation and its Executive Rule. This track did NOT fetch or exhaustively cross-check the repealed predecessor instruments' own article-by-article text against this Law's 391 articles (that would be a separate, much larger research effort outside this pass's scope of ingesting the primary in-force Law); only the repeal clause's own text and the secondary-source corroboration described above were checked, consistent with this pass's policy of 1-2 verification attempts per fact before flagging remaining uncertainty rather than over-investing further search effort.

Two further candidate secondary sources were attempted this pass in search of a third independent full-text cross-check specifically for the Articles-316-325 range flagged above: qistas.com's legislation-viewer page for this Law returned only a short, apparently access-gated preview (~2.6KB total, covering only Article 1's definitions in full and nothing beyond) when fetched directly; qanoniah.com's page for this Law is a JavaScript-rendered single-page application that returned no usable static article text via a direct HTTP fetch (only navigation-chrome text). Neither source could be used to further corroborate or contradict any article's text this pass; this track instead relies on the BOE-Arabic x BOE-official-English-translation two-source agreement documented in verification_methodology_note and in the nezams-duplicate-bug entry above for the disputed range, consistent with this pass's policy of not over-investing further search effort once a fact is adequately resolved.
